articleTitle: Business Intelligence and Learning Analytics as Contributors to a Data Driven Education Industry
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: In the fast pace of technological evolution, organizations need to become technology and data driven in order to be able to remain competitive in the future. The data is the core of this era, so they must be manipulated and utilized effectively in order to achieve the efficient use of technological tools and meet the desire goals. This change has affect education industry as well. The education institutions following this new reality must know what data they have and how they can use them. Their main source of the data is derived from students' learning experience; whether the student is participating in a face to face course or in an online course. Learning analytics is a concept of business intelligence that analyzes students learning data and present them in a meaningful manner. This research aims to study how learning analytics can be used as a part of a business intelligence system to support education institutions on how to understand the students and their study habits, and set a basic step on the paradigm of using the right data to get information, make decisions, and support the services that they offer.

articleTitle: Modern Software Programs for Cartometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to compare two software applications for the cartometric analysis (a quantitative assessment of the planimetric properties of old maps, their accuracy and specific distortions): the well-known program MapAnalyst (http://mapanalyst.org) and the lesser known Darcy (https://sourceforge.net/projects/jdarcy). As a result, it is shown that, in spite of the fact that MapAnalyst has a wider range of options, in some cases (for example, when analyzing such maps as that of Ptolemy) Darcy proves to be more convenient and effective.

articleTitle: Bioinformatics: Past and Present
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the history of emergence of a new discipline, bioinformatics. There is a whole range of approaches to define the subject of bioinformatics and describe its history. We directly link this discipline with the development of computer technologies and analysis of huge masses of biological information that began in the 1980s. The 1990s saw the rapid worldwide spread of bioinformatics when genome sequencing and mapping data for different species began to come fast like an avalanche. Scientists began to build up computerized databases to store this information. In the 2000s, these information bases were significantly improved and contained information not only on these giant molecules' sequences but also on their functionality. During the same period, DNA biochips (microarrays) began to be used to simultaneously measure expression of a large number of genes and to genotype multiple regions of a genome, and the Human Genome Project was completed. Presently, bioinformatics is a fast-growing separate discipline in its own right, with its own well-developed institutional basis.

Author Keywords: history of science, bioinformatics, genetic engineering, genomics, proteomics, biological data bases

articleTitle: The Struggle Against Cybernetics in the USSR and Its Influence on the Production of Computers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The article describes the dramatic events of the beginning of the computer industry in the USSR in 1950-1955, when the ideological struggle against "bourgeois pseudoscience cybernetics" practically stopped the production of computers in the USSR. The graph of the formerly secret report for the leadership of the USSR shows that by the end of 1954 there were 2319 computers of various types in the United States against 10 in the USSR. Recognition of cybernetics as a full-fledged science gave a powerful impetus to the development in the USSR of computer technology and electronics.

Author Keywords: Cybernetics, history of computing, Computer Science, ideological struggle, USSR

articleTitle: Innovative Digital Tools for Ecological Approaches in Urban Design in Slovak Context
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The impulses of information technology applications are nowadays manifested by the changes and innovations in a wide range of human activities, not excluding the urban design profession. Urban design is the process of creation of the aesthetic, social and environmental sustainable habitat. It is a multidisciplinary process that is specified by the planning, negotiations, communication with the stakeholders in the urban areas and looking for the consensus. The publication focuses on the technologies supporting digital creation and communication professionally related to architecture and urbanism. It explores the possibilities of actual geographical information technologies and spatial data infrastructures and how can they enhance the potential of effective urban design and participatory planning methods. Such approaches encompass significant asset to ecological approaches in urban design so as they can, if properly designed and coordinated, enhance the accessibility of actual and complex spatial information and the new communication methods. The experiences from Slovakia and European research networks on urban design are presented.

articleTitle: Effective GPU-Based Section Visualization in Isosurface of Saturation of Displacing Liquid in a Porous Medium
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: One of the methods for analysis of data obtained in computer simulation of the processes of unstable oil displacement is to visual analyze the plane sections of level surface (isosurface) of the saturation of a displacing viscous liquid in a sample of a porous medium. This paper presents an efficient distributed method for plane section visualization on a graphics processing unit (GPU) in a polygonal model of considered level surface. A polygonal model of clipped isosurface is created using a modified "marching cubes" method by means of the developed geometric and fragment shader programs. Based on the solutions proposed, a visualization program complex with an ergonomic user interface was implemented, which can be used in scientific researches, virtual laboratories, virtual environment systems, educational applications, etc.

Author Keywords: visualization, distributed computing, isosurface, oil displacement, GPU

articleTitle: 70 Years of Russian Computer Science
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: This article is devoted to the dramatic history of birth of the Soviet electronic computers. The central place is occupied by the history of creation of the first Soviet electronic computer M1 under the leadership of Isaac Brook. This computer was created in Moscow in the Energetic Institute of the Academy of Sciences by a small team of young engineers, students and technicians. Their further creative path is traced. Three of them later became general designers of the most powerful Soviet computers: Mikhail Kartsev, Nikolai Matyukhin, Yuri Rogachev. Tamara Alexandridi, Alexander Zalkind, Rene Shidlovsky, Julius Schrader became famous scientists. Julius Schrader later became also a well-known Catholic theologian.

Author Keywords: computer science, computing history, M1, MESM, Brook, Lebedev

articleTitle: Application of GIS-Technologies for Assessing the Disturbance of Natural Territories in the Construction of the Rybinsk Reservoir
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The Rybinsk Reservoir was filled in 1947. The application of methods of historical informatics with the use of GIS-technologies made it possible to assess the disturbance of natural territories changed due to the appearance of this reservoir. After filling the bowl of the Rybinsk Reservoir, a lot of people were relocated. The eighth part of the Yaroslavl land went under water. This territories include lots of villages and Mologa city, thousand hectares of the best floodplain meadows, cultivated arable lands, highly productive pastures, mushroom and berry forests. Analysis of data using GIS-technologies allows to form a basis for drawing up expert opinions and recommendations for further use.

articleTitle: The History of Science and Technology during the Transition to a Digital Economy
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The article is devoted to the application of digital technologies for the preservation of cultural and scientific heritage. Modern technologies brought about the development of new sub-disciplines of informatics that are associated with virtual reconstruction and preservation of objects. Another field of application of digital technologies in the history of science and technology can be foresight research, recognized as an effective method for determining priorities in the field of economy, science, technology. These works are a priority for the Institute of the History of Science and Technology.

Author Keywords: digital economy, technological revolution, informatics, foresight research, multidisciplinary research, history of science

articleTitle: On Calculating the Entropy of 2D Words Over a Finite Alphabet
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The objects of the article are finite 2D words over a finite alphabet. An efficient method for calculating the entropy function of 2D words is proposed. The algorithm adapts the window size. Possible applications of the entropy of finite 2D words in various domains are considered. Some recommendations concerning the choice of efficient policies of configuration storage.

Author Keywords: information entropy, 2D words over a finite alphabet, entropy function of 2D words, data storage

articleTitle: Analysis of Spontaneous Cryptocurrency Market
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The article describes a physical approach to the analysis of the spontaneous cryptocurrency market. The analytic method is developed and its application is described. In conclusion, the possibilities of control actions on the chaotic market are discussed.

Author Keywords: cryptocurrency, spontaneous market, physical model approach, control

articleTitle: Genesis of Russian Power Engineering
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The paper deals with the theoretical and practical foundations of Russian energy industry development. The article describes the first power plants, the main type of fuel (wood, oil and coal), the country's power machine-building and three main schools: electrical engineering, thermal engineering and hydraulic engineering. Energy scientists considered that the development of hydroelectricity would begin in European Russia: Volga, Dnieper and Northern water basins. In the thermal energy industry scientists decided to build the heat power station at the locations where fuel is extracted with energy transferred by electricity power lines. The first such plant was constructed near Bogorodsk between 1912 and 1914. A meeting held in Moscow in November 1915 on coal and peat in the Greater Moscow region was dedicated to the results of the first year of service of the Power Transmission plant. The greatest response was provoked by the report made by Krzhizhanovsky. The scientist set out the finalized strategic principles of the establishment of energy facilities in the country.

articleTitle: Development of Electrodeposition Industry in the USA (1900s–1950s): The Russian Outlook
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The paper reviews the development of electrodeposition industry in the USA in the first half of the 20th century as a separate, complex R&D industry characterized by the presence of essential components such as the systems for organizing research, manufacturing electroplating equipment, monitoring and control devices, and necessary chemicals, professional education, communications and information support. We have identified the main factors in the rapid growth of electrodeposition industry in the 1900s-1920s, and emphasized the contribution of American scientists and engineers to the development of basic technological processes of electroplating and to manufacturing automated equipment and monitoring and control devices. The paper highlights the role of the American Electroplaters' Society in attracting the scientists from adjacent disciplines as well as theoreticians in electrochemistry into tackling the problems of the applied electrochemical deposition. The most significant differences in the development of electroplating in the USSR and the USA during the period under study are identified.

articleTitle: Problems of Formation Area of the High-Capacity Accumulation of Electricity
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The problems of the development of the region of high-capacity energy storage devices that are not restricted by geographic location and, therefore, potentially suitable for mass production are considered. An assessment of this area is given as a set of key critical technologies for the entire global technosphere that are necessary in the implementation of the course for the intensive development of renewable energy sources (RES).

articleTitle: The Influence of the USSR on Chinese Engineering Education: Taking Beijing College of Aeronautics as an Example
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: When the People's Republic of China was founded in 1949, it was seriously lacking in scientific and technical professionals. For this reason, the Central Government reformed higher education, hired experts from the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe, and sent students and technicians overseas to socialist countries. The central government strengthened engineering education, established polytechnic universities or colleges, and engineering colleges such as iron and steel, mining, geology, machinery, and aviation. Universities or colleges generally adjusted their professional settings, implemented Soviet-style teaching plans, curriculum and syllabus, and translated Russian textbooks into Chinese. By 1953, 3/4 universities and colleges across the country had been adjusted. This paper, taking Beijing College of Aeronautics as an example, aims to discuss how the Soviet Union helped China to build higher engineering education, and promoted the transformation of the education model from versatile education practiced in Europe and the United States into professional model of the Soviet Union.

Author Keywords: PRC, education, higher education, USSR, Beijing College of Aeronautics, teaching, research

articleTitle: Development of Microelectronics and the Postwar Scientific and Technological Revolution
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The considerable scientific and technical advances in the second half of the twentieth century are associated with the invention of the transistor and the development of integrated microelectronics that contributed to the progress of computers. This has reflected in USSR novelties in computers, and on policies that recognized the high socioeconomic importance of that development in the early 60s'. In addition, scientists in Czechoslovakia, the USSR and other countries, influenced by the changes, promoted a new concept of "Scientific-Technological Revolution", in the 60s aimed to adapt society to the new environment. Much adaptations and innovations, both technological and economical are taking place in Russian electronics from the early 1990s, due to the continued technological revolutions and changes in economic structures.

articleTitle: The Use of Computer-Based Simulators to Train Cosmonauts for the Fulfillment of the Program of Scientific-Applied Research
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The progressive development of the Russian Segment of International Space Station (ISS RS) and putting the multi-functional laboratory module into operation on the Russian Segment lead both to an increase in the number of scientific-applied research and experiments (SAR), carried out by cosmonauts aboard the ISS, and to the actualization of ensuring the high quality of cosmonaut training for performing them. One of the ways of solving the problem is to upgrade technical facilities for cosmonaut training using digital information technologies. Theoretical studies of the problem of improving the efficiency of cosmonaut training for carrying out SAR aboard the ISS on the basis of computer technology are being conducted at the Gagarin Research&Test Cosmonaut Training Center (Gagarin R&T CTC) since 2006. The unique simulator complex, developed in 2013, is now actively used and upgraded. It comprises the dedicated stand to train cosmonauts for geophysical exploration and monitoring of the Earth's surface, automated workplaces for conducting aerial visual instrumental observations (VIOs), complex of functionalsimulation stands on the basis of computer-assisted virtual simulators of space experiments and scientific equipment using interactive 3D models (the "Nauka" complex). The said complex allows training cosmonauts for research on the space station, verifying flight data files and, also, improving techniques of performing space experiments.

articleTitle: Lukyanov's Hydraulic Integrator and Moor's Hydrocal: Experience in Applying of the Hydraulic Analogies Method in the USSR and the USA
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The method of hydraulic analogies and the respective devices began to be used in the USSR and the USA practically simultaneously. In the USSR, the hydrointegrator was created by V.S. Lukyanov in 1936 to study the mechanism of occurrence of temperature cracks in concrete during the construction of railway bridge supports. Afterwards, the design of the analog device was constantly being improved and Lukyanov's hydrointegrator became one of the first computers to be series-produced (1955). The studies have shown that up to occurrence of the computer the method of hydraulic analogies had been successfully used in the studies of various technological and natural processes. One of Lukyanov's hydrointegrators as well as some documents concerning its creator are deposited at the Polytechnic Museum. In the United States, a patent for a device using the method of hydraulic analogies, hydrocal, was issued to Arthur Moore in 1937. Hydrocal was intended for studying thermal processes. However, due to a number of shortcomings in the design, Moore's device was not widely applicable to solving engineering problems.

Author Keywords: method of hydraulic analogies, Lukyanov's hydraulic integrator, Moore's hydrocal

articleTitle: Digital Technologies as a Way to Popularize Museum Collections
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: This paper presents a general and novel approach and the results of the investigations in the field of museum technology based on 3D modeling, 3D video and 3D visualization. The described approach was used for making of 3D animation about showpieces of Peter the Great Anthropology and Ethnography Museum. A state-of-the-art approach based on digital technologies provides new opportunities for studying objects of the past, history, national traditions.

articleTitle: Unmanned Remote-Controlled Military Aircraft – Early Attempts
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The article is devoted to the first work on unmanned remote-controlled aircraft in Germany and in the USSR. It gives also information about an attempt to use Russian aircraft-bomb in the beginning of Second World war.

articleTitle: Data Mining Methods and Techniques for Fault Detection and Predictive Maintenance in Housing and Utility Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: Recent development of new approaches to data collection, storage and analysis make the data-driven condition monitoring techniques a powerful instrument in housing and utility infrastructure maintenance. Advancements in software development and sensor construction lead to spread of "Internet of Things" concept suggesting the devices to be equipped with various sensors producing large amount of data. The paper introduces an architecture of the information system for predictive maintenance in housing and utility infrastructure based on scalable distributed computing and data mining methods for fault detection and prognostics. Data mining methods featured in the information system are compared and analyzed.

Author Keywords: internet of things, data analysis, predictive maintenance, fault detection, housing and utility infrastructure

articleTitle: Collection "Mathematical Analogue Devices" of Polytechnic Museum
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The collection "Mathematical analogue devices" of the Polytechnic Museum includes a vast class of devices that developed and improved in direct contact with the development of many fundamental and applied sciences: mathematics, mechanics, as well as drawing, geodesy and cartography. Domestic scientists have a number of discoveries and inventions in this field that are not sufficiently known or undeservedly forgotten. These inventions are the Bibikov's agrometer, the Ermakov's and Zarubin's planimeters, the harmonic analyser of Martens, combined devices of Shtykan and others. At present, in this collection, depending on the kind of the tasks to be solved, the following groups of devices can be distinguished: planimeters, integrimeters, degree planimeters, harmonic analysers, Stieltjes-planimeters, integraphs, combined devices.

Author Keywords: museum, collection, mathematical, analogue, device, integral, instrument, planimeter, integrimeter, integrator, integraph, harmonic analyser

articleTitle: Kition Planetarium and Observatory (Cyprus) in International Research Programs Concerning NEOs
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: Observations of Near Earth Objects (NEOs) became an important part of astronomy. Meteor showers and fireballs are being monitored yearly by the Kition Planetarium and Observatory. Data are shared with observatories from other countries and the International Meteor Organization. Educational programs developed by the organization are providing attendees the skills for meteor and asteroid observations. Results of international research programs and participation in meteor and asteroid observations are widely used in public outreach. The international collaboration is described in details on the example of flyby of fireball over Cyprus on the 8th September 2016.

Author Keywords: Asteroids, minor bodies, Near Earth Object, Near Earth Asteroid, Solar system exploration, Planet formation, IMO, fireball event 3334 2016, Kition Planetarium and Observatory

articleTitle: Russian Virtual Museum of the IT History
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: Russian Virtual Computer Museum (RVCM) has been steadily becoming more and more famous, both in Russia and worldwide, for last twenty years - the RVCM site maintains English language version as well. From 1.5 to 2 thousand people visit the RVCM site daily. Besides collecting and processing historical materials on computing and informatics RVCM regularly organises international conferences and publish books on the history of computer and information science. In comparison with other computer (on-line) museums RVCM possesses most comprehensive digital on-line collection of articles, books, individual memories and other materials on the history of Soviet computing.

Author Keywords: history, computer, informatics, programming, algorithmic languages, IMS, ERP-systems
